text:
josh: Quick follow-up from the loader spike: instead of a JSON header blob I'm leaning toward a compact TLV-style binary header inside safetensors to minimize parse time and size. Thoughts?

maria: TLV makes sense for perf. We still need versioning and forward/backward compatibility rules. Suggest a 4-byte magic, 2-byte version, 2-byte header_len, then TLVs. Keep total header <= 6KB ideally.

kevin: Agreed. If we make TLV types extensible we can add proto fields later. Important TLVs: SHARD_ID (string), WARMUP_RANGES (list of pairs), DIGEST (sha256), SIG_METADATA (signature reference), TRUST_POLICY (enum: none/namespace/global).

sara: Security: signature must be verifiable by runtime via public key bundle or KMS. For Dedicated/Private we can allow "trust-on-namespace" but hosted should default to manifest verification only.

josh: Failure modes we observed in spike: 1) header present but digest mismatch -> runtime should refuse to trust header and fall back to manifest. 2) partial header read (truncated file) -> identify via header_len and abort warmup. 3) header claims ranges but origin doesn't support range GET -> fall back to whole-shard fetch.

maria: UX question: how do we surface header trust decision in telemetry? Proposal: header_detected, header_trusted, manifest_checked, reconcile_status (ok/mismatch/absent). Tag records with namespace and origin type.

kevin: Implementation note for loader state machine: OPEN -> read fixed prefix -> if header_len > 0 read header -> parse TLVs -> produce synchronous WarmupPlan (best-effort) -> schedule async manifest fetch -> if manifest arrives and verify(digest) then reconcile: if ranges differ by > X% evict warmed pages and rewarm.

ops-bot: Note: perf test job 4123 created: warmup/header-vs-manifest (run on canary infra) https://ci.redwood/jobs/4123

sara: Migration path: publishers can start embedding header v1 while also publishing sidecar manifest. Runtimes enable TRUST_EMBEDDED_HEADER via feature flag. After 3 weeks of telemetry where header_trusted=true and reconcile_status=ok >=95% we can consider promoting to default in Dedicated. Hosted will remain conservative longer.

josh: Example tiny TLV hex (illustrative):
<magic> 52 57 4D 50 | <ver> 00 01 | <len> 00 2C | TLV(type=0x01,len=0x07) 73 68 61 72 64 2D 31 | TLV(type=0x02,len=0x10) 00 00 00 00 00 01 00 00 00 00 02 00 00 00 00 03
(meaning: magic RWMP ver1, shard-id="shard-1", three warmup ranges)

maria: Nice. Also consider a small bitmap TLV for "first K tensors hot" which is cheap to encode and useful for common LLM layouts where first few embeddings + layers matter.

kevin: Edge case: publishers may want to update warmup priorities without republishing weights. That's where sidecar manifests win. Header should only contain stable, transport-safe hints; ephemeral rollout metadata stays in manifest. Document this in ABI.

sara: Ops/Security checklist: signing format, public key rollover, runtime opt-in flag, telemetry retention policy, and a test harness to attempt header-poisoning attacks.

josh: I'll draft a short RFC with TLV spec, state machine, example encodings and a migration checklist. Owners: josh(spec + perf), kevin(loader), maria(telemetry), sara(security). Will link RFC when ready.

ops-bot: RFC draft PR #2410 opened: https://git.redwood/eng/rfcs/2410

maria: Let's try to run perf job 4123 and review numbers before enabling the flag in canary.

josh: Good plan. Thanks all.
